1.0    BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE

Kairos Power, LLC., (Kairos) began pre-application discussions with the U.S. Nuclear
Regulatory Commission (NRC) staff on its proposed Kairos Power Fluoride-Salt-Cooled, High-
Temperature Reactor (KP-FHR) in October 2018. In December 2020, Kairos announced that
the Hermes test reactor would be used to support the future development of the KP-FHR.
Kairos was issued a construction permit (CP) on December 14, 2023, for the Hermes 1 test
reactor to be located at a site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee (Agencywide Documents Access and
Management System (ADAMS) Accession No. ML23338A260). Kairos was issued two CPs on
November 21, 2024, for the Hermes 2 test reactor facility located at an adjacent site
(ML24324A019).

By letter dated July 11, 2025, Kairos submitted KP-TR-026-NP, “Operator Training and Testing
Program for the Non-Power Kairos Power Fluoride Salt-Cooled High-Temperature Reactors,”
(ML25192A231). By letter dated July 30, 2025, Kairos submitted requests for exemptions from
certain requirements in Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part 55,
“Operators’ Licenses” (ML25211A317). The NRC staff determined that the topical report (TR)
and exemption request presented sufficient information to begin a detailed technical review
(ML25210A446 and ML25273A286).

The NRC staff issued an audit plan on January 13, 2026 (ML25339A165). The purpose of the
audit was for the NRC staff to gain a better understanding of KP-TR-026-NP and the associated
exemptions by providing an opportunity to review and discuss material used to support
                                                -2-


statements or conclusions in the TR and exemption requests. Since the TR and exemption
requests are related and being reviewed in parallel, the NRC staff conducted a single regulatory
audit for both licensing actions.

2.0       AUDIT REGULATORY BASES

The TR requests the NRC staff review and approval of an initial licensed operator training and
testing program as well as the licensed operator requalification program. Therefore, the basis
for the audit includes the regulatory requirements in 10 CFR Part 55, which establish
procedures and criteria for the issuance of licenses to operators and senior operators for
utilization facilities. The TR also describes the simulation facility used for conducting the
operating tests. Simulation facility requirements are described in 10 CFR 55.46, “Simulation
facilities.” The requested exemptions are also from various requirements in 10 CFR Part 55.

3.0       AUDIT OBJECTIVES

The primary objective of the audit was to enable a more effective and efficient review of
KP-TR-026-NP and the associated exemptions through the NRC staff’s review of supporting
documentation and discussions with Kairos. A secondary purpose of the audit was to identify
any information that will require docketing to support the NRC staff’s safety evaluations.

4.0       AUDIT ACTIVITIES

The audit was conducted from February 2026, through September 2026, via the Kairos
electronic reading room (eRR). The NRC staff conducted the audit in accordance with the Office
of Nuclear Reactor Regulation (NRR) Office Instruction LIC-111, Revision 1, “Regulatory Audits”
(ML19226A274).

Members of the audit team were selected based on their detailed knowledge of the subject
matter and are listed below:

      •   Amy Beasten - Reactor Engineer, Audit Lead
      •   Michele DeSouza - Reactor Engineer
      •   Lauren Nist - Reactor Engineer
      •   Theresa Buchanan - Senior Reactor Engineer
      •   Pravin Sawant - Senior Nuclear Engineer
      •   Cayetano Santos Jr. - Senior Project Manager
      •   Scott Tonsfeldt – Technical Assistant

The NRC staff reviewed the following items via the eRR:

      •   Presentation slides providing responses to audit questions
      •   Draft TR and exemption change package markups
      •   Kairos Power, KP-1000007250, Revision 0, “Hermes Operator Training Simulator
          Description and Architecture,” issued July 2025
      •   Kairos Power, KP-1000007889, Revision 0, “Simulation Facility Performance Testing
          and Fidelity Program,” issued July 2025
      •   Kairos Power, HER-TR-001, Revision 3, “Initial Licensed Operator Training and Testing
          Program for the Kairos Power Hermes Reactor Facility,” issued March 2026
                                                -3-


      •   Kairos Power, KP-1000007872, Revision 1, “Operator Licensing Examination Question
          Writing Guide,” issued December 2025
      •   Kairos Power, HER-TR-002, Revision 3, “Licensed Operator Requalification Program for
          the Kairos power Hermes Reactor Facility,” issued March 2026
      •   Kairos Power, KP-1000007871, Revision 1, “Licensing Examination Security,” issued
          December 2025

The NRC staff transmitted audit questions to Kairos on January 13, 2026 (ML25339A165).

5.0       SUMMARY OF AUDIT OUTCOME

The NRC staff audit focused on the review of supporting documents associated with the topics
identified in the audit plan and subsequently transmitted questions. The NRC staff reviewed
information through the eRR and held discussions with Kairos staff to understand and resolve
questions. In many cases, Kairos updated KP-TR-026-NP and the associated exemption
requests to resolve items discussed during the audit. Gaining access to underlying
documentation and engaging in audit discussions about various aspects of the TR and
exemption requests facilitated the NRC staff’s understanding and aided in assessing the
proposed methodology and basis for the exemptions. The table in the enclosure reproduces the
transmitted audit questions and summarizes the resolution of the questions.

As noted in the enclosure, Kairos updated the TR and exemption requests based on the audit
discussions. These updates are included in Revision 1 of the TR and exemption requests, which
were submitted in a letter dated October 7, 2026 (ML26280A101).

6.0       EXIT BRIEFING

The NRC staff conducted an audit exit meeting on September 28, 2026. At the exit meeting, the
NRC staff reiterated the purpose of the audit and discussed their activities.

7.0       ADDITIONAL INFORMATION RESULTING FROM AUDIT

As a result of the audit, the NRC staff did not identify any requests for additional information
related to this TR. However, Kairos revised the subject TR and exemption requests to address
